{"self_assessment": "Impact: I owned the bottom line of the fish, which is stroke 2 on the pad. I traced it from the nose so it was connected to the start, and the bottom outline was live to the crossing. In the last third I took on the fork's inner notch, the last open spot in the picture. I laid the join from the fork into the notch's upper open end, then moved on to the lower open end in the final seconds. That notch is what lets the tail read as a fork.

Execution: I picked one piece of work and stayed on it. I laid the bottom line in steady short batches. I inspected the notch closely twice before building, so I joined the right two open ends instead of guessing. When the shared pile ran low I asked for spare and stray dominoes, which kept me building through the final minutes.

Collaboration: I worked out the bottom-line meeting point with Leo, so we joined in the middle of the run. I told the others plainly when I was working in the notch and asked them to keep clear. That avoided bumps in the tightest spot. I took Priya's offer of spare dominoes and asked Tom, Leo and Priya to send me the pale strays. I also sent a clear status summary to the whole table at the midpoint.

Leadership: I took ownership of the hardest remaining gap and kept the table informed about it. I told people which spots to stay off and which jobs they could go ahead with, such as Leo's jam on the upper tail. That left the others free to finish their own pieces. I'd put my share of the result at a bit above an even split, since the bottom outline and the notch joins were mine.", "my_share_percent": 30}
